page.layout: One page of text, one column, running head at top, page number at top right. Continuation of a prayer from the previous page, then a passage in italic lines, ending with FINIS and a printed motto. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: rus, quæ petimus, quia hæ sunt causæ cur id faciat: Tuæ gloriæ seruiet, ergo facies: quia gloria tua tibi est curæ. Tu es Rex optimus, ergo dabis ea tuis subditis. Tu es potentissimus, ergo tuam potentiam ostendes in dandis his donis, quæ sunt maxima, & quæ á nullo alio, quàm à te solo possunt dari.
Amen. Hoc adiungitur, non vt pars precationis, sed

p.i: 1. Quia hæc particula notat desiderium, ac votum verum & sincerum, quo optamus, vt exaudiamur

main_text.p: 2. Quia hæc eadem particula notat certitudinem seu professionem fiduciæ, vel confessionem & confirmationem fidei nostræ, qua confidimus nos exauditum iri. Igitur Amen significat, 1. fiat, ac certum ratum q; sit quod petimus, & petitioni nostræ Deus respondeat. 2. Vere ac certè nos Deus, suæ promissionis non immemor, exaudias.

page.notes: The handwritten ink line "SOLI DEO SIT GLORIA" below the printed motto is manuscript and is omitted. The first word "rus," is a fragment from the line above the page top. The paragraph beginning "Amen." is set with a leading italic word and a mark after it that is hard to read; it is transcribed as "Amen." The numbered italic passage is set in short indented lines; its line breaks are simplified and the numbered items "1." and "2." are kept as printed. "q; sit" in "ratum q; sit" is uncertain (the printed form may be qz/qs), so it should be checked against the scan.
